action.message:
I was unable to land the behavioral fix. During this session I accidentally removed the `return True` line from `ModelAdmin.lookup_allowed()` in django/contrib/admin/options.py, then restored the file to its original state. My subsequent attempts to apply the actual fix were rejected as "old_str equals new_str" because I mistakenly submitted identical old/new strings, and I ran out of requests before making a real change.

Current state: django/contrib/admin/options.py is back to the original upstream code (the broken `if len(relation_parts) <= 1:` block was repaired to include `return True`). Public regression tests pass (162 tests, OK), but the target feature behavior — `lookup_allowed('restaurant__place__country', ...)` returning True when a ForeignKey/OneToOneField is the primary key — is NOT fixed. Host feature acceptance will fail.

The intended fix (not applied): in the loop, only skip appending `part` to `relation_parts` when the field is not itself a relation, i.e. change the condition so a relational field that happens to be in `prev_field.path_infos[-1].target_fields` (like a OneToOneField primary key) is still added to `relation_parts`, preventing the incorrect concrete-inheritance shortcut.
